title: Smith v. Mississippi Valley Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained the complaint only insofar as Presbytery erroneously judged that Jeremy Smith had refused to appear, and reversed that judgment. It did not sustain the other four allegations or the remainder of the fifth. Because other grounds supported excommunication and the erroneous finding's effect was unclear, the SJC declined to annul the censure; Presbytery could consider whether to modify it.
first_summary: Ministers challenged Jeremy Smith's excommunication, arguing that Presbytery improperly found him incorrigible and contumacious. The SJC sustained the complaint only as to Presbytery's finding that he refused to appear: absence after a committee email was not refusal of a Presbytery citation. It reversed that finding but left the excommunication intact because other grounds existed and the finding's effect on the censure was unclear.
summary: Ministers challenged Jeremy Smith's excommunication, but not his deposition. The SJC rejected four allegations and most of the fifth, holding among other things that two ignored citations are only one possible form of contumacy. It sustained the complaint solely because Presbytery wrongly treated Smith's absence as a refusal to appear: a committee email was not a citation by Presbytery. The SJC reversed that finding but did not annul the excommunication, leaving Presbytery to consider whether modification was necessary.
